title: Listening practice: A Kite, a Magnet, and a Class Survey
description: Three short clips to listen to twice: a narrated story, a science test, and a class survey with a claim.

stimuli.title: Listen: A kite at the park

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Last Saturday, Mei went to the park with her brother Tomás. They brought a red kite. At first, the wind was too weak, so the kite stayed on the grass. Then Tomás ran fast across the field, and the kite lifted up into the sky. Suddenly, the string broke! The kite flew over the trees. Mei and Tomás felt sad. But a kind man found the kite and brought it back to them.

stimuli.script: Narrator: Last Saturday, Mei went to the park with her brother Tomás. They brought a red kite. At first, the wind was too weak, so the kite stayed on the grass. Then Tomás ran fast across the field, and the kite lifted up into the sky. Suddenly, the string broke! The kite flew over the trees. Mei and Tomás felt sad. But a kind man found the kite and brought it back to them.

stimuli.title: Listen: Testing a magnet

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Today we will test a magnet. First, I hold the magnet near a paper clip. The paper clip jumps to the magnet! That happens because the paper clip is made of steel, and steel has iron in it. Magnets pull on iron. Next, I try a plastic spoon. Nothing happens, because plastic is not metal. Last, I try a piece of aluminum foil. Foil is metal, but nothing happens, because foil has no iron in it.

stimuli.script: Teacher: Today we will test a magnet. First, I hold the magnet near a paper clip. The paper clip jumps to the magnet! That happens because the paper clip is made of steel, and steel has iron in it. Magnets pull on iron. Next, I try a plastic spoon. Nothing happens, because plastic is not metal. Last, I try a piece of aluminum foil. Foil is metal, but nothing happens, because foil has no iron in it.

stimuli.title: Listen: Our class survey

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Hello, everyone. Today my partner and I will share our class survey. We asked twenty-four students which pet they like best. Ten students chose dogs. Eight students chose cats. Four students chose fish, and two students chose birds. So dogs got the most votes, and birds got the fewest. My partner, Ben, says cats and fish together beat dogs. Let me check. Eight plus four is twelve, and twelve is more than ten. So Ben is right.

stimuli.script: Amara: Hello, everyone. Today my partner and I will share our class survey. We asked twenty-four students which pet they like best. Ten students chose dogs. Eight students chose cats. Four students chose fish, and two students chose birds. So dogs got the most votes, and birds got the fewest. My partner, Ben, says cats and fish together beat dogs. Let me check. Eight plus four is twelve, and twelve is more than ten. So Ben is right.

items.stem: Why did the kite stay on the grass at first?

options.text: The kite was stuck in the trees.
The kite was too big for Mei.

distractors.a: The string broke later, after the kite was already flying.
distractors.c: The kite flew over the trees after the string broke, not before.
distractors.d: Nobody says the kite is big. This detail is not in the clip.

items.explanation: The narrator says that at first the wind was too weak, so the kite stayed on the grass.

support.clue: Listen for the words 'at first' and 'so'. The reason comes just before the word 'so'.
support.frame: At first, the kite stayed on the grass because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. Listen to this sentence: 'The picnic moved inside because it started to rain.' The reason comes after the word because. Now listen to the kite clip and find the reason the kite did not fly at first.

misconceptions.a: mixes up the order of events
misconceptions.c: puts an event at the wrong time
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that was not said

items.text: The kite stayed on the grass.
A kind man brought the kite back.

items.explanation: The kite stayed down at first, then Tomás ran, then the string broke, and finally a kind man brought the kite back.

support.clue: Listen for time words such as 'at first', 'then', and 'suddenly'. Each one starts a new event.
support.frame: At first, ______. Then, ______. Suddenly, ______. At the end, ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'First, Ana filled the bucket. Then she carried it to the garden. Suddenly, the handle came off. At the end, she held the bucket with both arms.' Each time word starts a new event. Put the kite events in order the same way.

items.stem: How did Mei and Tomás feel when the kite flew away?

distractors.a: The kite flew high before the string broke, but the clip says they felt sad after it flew away.
distractors.b: The kind man helped later, after the kite flew away. The clip says they felt sad at that moment.
distractors.c: The wind was weak at first, not strong. The clip never says they were worried about the wind.

items.explanation: After the string broke and the kite flew over the trees, the narrator says Mei and Tomás felt sad.

support.clue: Listen to what happens just after the word 'suddenly'. The narrator names the feeling in the next two sentences.
support.frame: When the kite flew away, Mei and Tomás felt ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'The soup spilled, and Leo felt upset.' The storyteller names the feeling right after the problem. Listen for the feeling word right after the kite's problem.

misconceptions.a: remembers an earlier moment instead of this one
misconceptions.b: puts an event at the wrong time
misconceptions.c: adds a detail that was not said

items.stem: According to the teacher, why does the paper clip jump to the magnet?

distractors.b: The teacher says the foil is metal too, but the magnet does not pull it. Being metal is not the reason.
distractors.c: Plastic is the spoon, and the magnet does not pull it.
distractors.d: The teacher never talks about size.

items.explanation: The teacher says the paper clip is steel, steel has iron in it, and magnets pull on iron.

support.clue: Listen for the word 'because' right after the paper clip jumps. The reason comes next.
support.frame: The paper clip jumps to the magnet because it ______.
support.model: Mentor example. Listen to this sentence: 'The puddle is gone because the sun was hot.' The reason comes right after because. Now listen to the magnet clip and find the reason for the paper clip.

misconceptions.b: thinks all metal is pulled by a magnet
misconceptions.d: uses an idea that is not in the clip

facts: Magnets attract iron and steel, and steel contains iron.

items.stem: Match each object to what the teacher says about it.

right.text: Is not pulled; it is plastic
Is not pulled; it is metal

items.explanation: The paper clip is steel, so the magnet pulls it. The spoon is plastic, so the magnet does not pull it. The foil is metal, but the magnet does not pull it.

support.clue: Listen to the three tests in order: the paper clip, the plastic spoon, and the aluminum foil. Notice what happens each time.
support.frame: When the teacher tried the ______, the magnet ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'When Rosa tried the red pen, it wrote clearly. When she tried the old marker, it left no line.' Each object is joined to what happened. Do the same with the three objects in the magnet clip.

facts: Plastic is not metal and is not pulled by a magnet.
Aluminum is a metal, but a magnet does not pull it.

items.stem: Which two sentences are true about the test?

options.text: The magnet pulled the paper clip.
The magnet pulled the plastic spoon.
The aluminum foil has iron in it.

distractors.b: The teacher says nothing happens with the plastic spoon.
distractors.d: The teacher says foil is metal, but it has no iron in it.

items.explanation: The paper clip jumps to the magnet. The foil is metal, but it has no iron, so the magnet does not pull it.

support.clue: Listen to each object in turn. For each one, ask: did the magnet pull it? Is it metal?
support.frame: The magnet pulled the ______, but it did not pull the ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'The sponge soaked up the juice, but it did not soak up the sand.' Two true sentences can tell what did and did not happen. Choose the two true sentences about the magnet test.

facts: Aluminum foil is metal, but a magnet does not pull it.

items.stem: How many more students chose dogs than fish?

distractors.a: Four is how many students chose fish, not the difference.
distractors.b: Eight is how many students chose cats.
distractors.d: Fourteen is ten plus four. The question asks how many more, so you subtract.

items.explanation: Ten students chose dogs and four chose fish, and 10 - 4 = 6.

support.clue: Write down the votes for dogs and the votes for fish. The words 'how many more' ask you to compare the two numbers.
support.frame: Dogs got ______ votes and fish got ______ votes, so the difference is ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Twelve children rode bikes and five rode scooters. To find how many more rode bikes, subtract: twelve minus five is seven.' Compare the two numbers the same way for the survey.

misconceptions.a: reports one number instead of comparing

items.stem: Ben says cats and fish together beat dogs. Which fact supports his claim?

options.text: Cats and fish together got ten votes, and dogs got twelve.
Cats and fish together got twelve votes, and dogs got ten.
Dogs got more votes than any other single pet in the survey.
Birds got the fewest votes of any pet in the whole survey.

distractors.a: This swaps the numbers. The speaker says cats and fish together got twelve votes, and dogs got ten.
distractors.c: This is true, but it compares dogs with one pet at a time. It does not compare dogs with cats and fish together.
distractors.d: This is true, but it says nothing about cats and fish together.

items.explanation: Ben's claim compares cats and fish together with dogs. Eight plus four is twelve, which is more than the ten votes for dogs.

support.clue: Listen for the numbers Ben and Amara compare.
support.frame: A fact that supports the claim compares ______ with ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Maya says the red team scored more than the blue team. Her evidence: red scored nine points and blue scored six.' Evidence for a comparison uses both numbers. Now think about which fact fits Ben's comparison.

misconceptions.c: uses a true fact that does not compare the groups
misconceptions.d: uses a true fact that does not support the claim
